top_candidates.subject: [MemorySSA] Fix handling of cross-iteration dependencies for calls (#187291)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This MemorySSA change threads a new cross-iteration-awareness flag through the clobber-walker’s def-path bookkeeping and verification logic. The walker now records whether a path may cross loop iterations, propagates that state when re-queuing searches through MemoryPhi nodes, and uses it to scope alias queries during clobber sanity checks. A new MemorySSA test specifically covers a loop-carried call/memcpy dependency to ensure the clobber is attributed to the loop phi rather than liveOnEntry.
Changed symbols: checkClobberSanity; ClobberWalker; ClobberWalker::DefPath; ClobberWalker::addSearches; MemorySSA; BatchAACrossIterationScope; instructionClobbersQuery; call-loop-carried-dependency.ll
Behavioral change: Adds a MayBeCrossIteration bit to clobber-walker paths so loop-carried dependencies are tracked distinctly from same-iteration paths.; Propagates cross-iteration state when expanding MemoryPhi and def-chain searches.; Wraps verification alias queries in a cross-iteration AA scope when the queried path may span iterations.; Adjusts sanity checking to use the MemoryLocation carried by the path object rather than the old pair field layout.

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_IV:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds [260 x i8], ptr [[TMP]], i64 0, i64 [[IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:  ; 1 = MemoryDef(3)->3 - clobbered by 3 = MemoryPhi({entry,liveOnEntry},{while.body,1})
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i8 42, ptr [[TMP_IV]], align 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[C]], label %[[WHILE_BODY]], label %[[EXIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP_IV_1:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr [[TMP_IV]], i64 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SUB7:%.*]] = sub nsw i64 259, [[IV]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:  ; 2 = MemoryDef(1)->3 - clobbered by 3 = MemoryPhi({entry,liveOnEntry},{while.body,1})
+; CHECK-NEXT:    call void @llvm.memcpy.p0.p0.i64(ptr align 1 [[NAME]], ptr nonnull align 1 [[TMP_IV_1]], i64 [[SUB7]], i1 false)
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %tmp = alloca [260 x i8], align 16
+  br label %while.body
+
+while.body:
+  %iv = phi i64 [ %iv.next, %while.body ], [ 259, %entry ]
+  %iv.next = add nsw i64 %iv, -1
+  %tmp.iv = getelementptr inbounds [260 x i8], ptr %tmp, i64 0, i64 %iv

+  br i1 %c, label %while.body, label %exit
+

+  %tmp.iv.1 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %tmp.iv, i64 1

top_candidates.subject: [LICM] Improve hoist-safety checks for dominated MemorySSA accesses (#169379)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This LICM change tightens MemorySSA-based hoist-safety checks by skipping MemorySSA accesses that are already dominated by the instruction being analyzed, but only when the transformation is not a sink. The patch is localized to LICM's conflict-checking logic and is accompanied by LICM tests around inaccessible-memory call hoisting, indicating a refinement in how MemorySSA dominance is used to decide whether a memory access can be treated as conflicting.
Changed symbols: noConflictingReadWrites; MemorySSA; MSSA->dominates; Flags.getIsSink; LICM
Behavioral change: Adds an early-continue for MemorySSA accesses dominated by the current instruction when not sinking, reducing the set of accesses considered conflicting.; Changes the invariant from 'scan all accesses' to 'ignore dominated accesses in non-sink hoist checks', which can alter MemorySSA dependence reasoning used by LICM.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA; ClobberWalker; verifyOptResult; OtherClobbers; MSSA.dominates
Reproducer link: crash/assertion at -O1; MemorySSA clobber-walker verification failure
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/LICM.cpp; MemorySSA-backed scalar optimization
Causal explanation: The issue is specifically about a MemorySSA clobber-walker verification assertion, and this commit directly changes LICM's use of MemorySSA dominance in hoist-safety checks. That makes it plausibly related because an incorrect dominance-based skip could change which memory accesses LICM treats as clobbers, potentially affecting MemorySSA verification. However, the retrieved hunk only shows a conservative filtering rule in LICM, not the verifier or clobber walker itself, so the link is indirect rather than definitive.
Causal confidence: 0.74
Build risk: Touches a high-risk optimizer pass (LICM) that depends on MemorySSA correctness.; Behavior depends on dominance relationships and sink/hoist mode, which are subtle and test-sensitive.; Includes new LICM test coverage for inaccessible-memory call hoisting, suggesting the change is intended to affect memory-dependence reasoning.

+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP]], label %[[LOOP]], label %[[AFTER_LOOP:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[AFTER_LOOP]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[ACC_LCSSA:%.*]] = phi i32 [ [[ACC]], %[[LOOP]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i32 [[ACC_LCSSA]]
+;
+entry:
+  br label %loop
+loop:
+  %phi = phi ptr [ %start, %entry ], [ %gep, %loop ]
+  %load = load i32, ptr %phi
+  %val = call i32 @fn_args(i32 %load)
+  call void @fn_write_inaccessible_mem()
+  call void @fn_read_inaccessible_mem(i32 %load)
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds nuw i32, ptr %phi, i64 %x

Summary: This commit adds loop-kind metadata handling so diagnostics can distinguish plain, vectorized, and epilogue loops when reporting leftover transformations. It introduces a helper to derive a loop-kind prefix from loop metadata and threads that prefix into unroll and missed-transformation warnings, plus adds tests for the new remark text.
Changed symbols: llvm::getLoopVectorizeKindPrefix; llvm::UnrollLoop; warnAboutLeftoverTransformations; LoopUnroll; WarnMissedTransforms; LoopTransformWarning; vectorizer-loop-kind-unroll-warning.ll
Behavioral change: Derives a textual prefix from loop metadata flags llvm.loop.vectorize.body and llvm.loop.vectorize.epilogue.; Changes unroll diagnostics to say 'vectorized loop' or 'epilogue loop' when applicable.; Changes missed-unroll warnings to include the same loop-kind prefix.; Adds tests asserting distinct warnings for plain, vectorized, and epilogue loops.
Assertion or trace link: No MemorySSA; No ClobberWalker; No verifyOptResult; No OtherClobbers; No MSSA.dominates
Reproducer link: No -O1 crash reproduction evidence; No MemorySSA verification assertion evidence
Pass or subsystem link: LoopVectorize; LoopUnroll; WarnMissedTransforms; LoopTransformWarning
Causal explanation: The visible change is diagnostic/remark text for loop transformation warnings and metadata classification of vectorized/epilogue loops. It does not alter MemorySSA, clobber walking, or dominance queries, so the hunk provides no direct causal path to the reported MemorySSA verification crash.
Causal confidence: 0.93

--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/LoopTransformWarning/vectorizer-loop-kind-unroll-warning.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,120 @@
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='loop-vectorize,loop-unroll,transform-warning' \
+; RUN:   -force-vector-width=4 -force-vector-interleave=1 \
+; RUN:   -enable-epilogue-vectorization -epilogue-vectorization-force-VF=4 \
+; RUN:   -disable-output -pass-remarks-missed=transform-warning 2>&1 | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='loop-vectorize,loop-unroll,transform-warning' \
+; RUN:   -force-vector-width=4 -force-vector-interleave=1 \
+; RUN:   -enable-epilogue-vectorization -epilogue-vectorization-force-VF=4 \
+; RUN:   -disable-output -pass-remarks-output=%t.yaml 2>&1
+; RUN: FileCheck --input-file=%t.yaml %s --check-prefix=YAML
+
+; Verify that when the loop vectorizer produces body / epilogue
+; metadata and the unroller *fails* to unroll (runtime unrolling is disabled),
+; the surviving unroll hints reach WarnMissedTransforms, which emits a
+; distinct "not unrolled" warning for each loop-kind qualifier.
+;
+; Pipeline: loop-vectorize -> loop-unroll -> transform-warning.
+; Epilogue vectorization is forced to exercise all four loop categories:
+;
+;   1. plain loop         – not touched by the vectorizer
+;   2. vectorized loop    – main vector body      (has vectorize.body)
+;   3. epilogue loop      – epilogue loop          (has vectorize.epilogue)
+;
+; Runtime unrolling is disabled via metadata so the unroller cannot act,
+; causing the pragma-unroll hint to survive to the warning pass.
+; Both stderr warnings and YAML structured output are checked.
+
+;--- plain_loop: vectorize.enable=false, runtime unroll disabled ---------------
+
+; CHECK:     warning: test.cpp:1:1: loop not unrolled: the optimizer was unable to perform the requested transformation
+; CHECK-NOT: warning: test.cpp:1:1: vectorized
+; CHECK-NOT: warning: test.cpp:1:1: epilogue
+
+define void @plain_loop(ptr noalias %A, i64 %n) !dbg !100 {
+entry:
+  br label %loop, !dbg !108
+loop:
+  %i = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%i.next, %loop]
+  %gep = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i64 %i
+  %v = load i32, ptr %gep, align 4
+  %add = add i32 %v, 1
+  store i32 %add, ptr %gep, align 4
+  %i.next = add nuw nsw i64 %i, 1
+  %cmp = icmp slt i64 %i.next, %n
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %exit, !dbg !108, !llvm.loop !10
+exit:
+  ret void
+}
+
+;--- vectorizable_loop: vectorized with epilogue, all three fail to unroll -----
+
+; CHECK-DAG: warning: test.cpp:10:1: vectorized loop not unrolled: the optimizer was unable to perform the requested transformation
+; CHECK-DAG: warning: test.cpp:10:1: epilogue loop not unrolled: the optimizer was unable to perform the requested transformation
+
+define void @vectorizable_loop(ptr noalias %A, ptr noalias %B, i64 %n) !dbg !200 {
+entry:
+  br label %loop, !dbg !208
+loop:
+  %i = phi i64 [0, %entry], [%i.next, %loop]
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i64 %i
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i64 %i
+  %v = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %add = add i32 %v, 1
+  store i32 %add, ptr %gep.b, align 4
+  %i.next = add nuw nsw i64 %i, 1
+  %cmp = icmp slt i64 %i.next, %n
+  br i1 %cmp, label %loop, label %exit, !dbg !208, !llvm.loop !20
+exit:
+  ret void
+}
+
+;--- YAML checks ---------------------------------------------------------------
+
+; YAML:      --- !Failure
+; YAML:      Pass:            transform-warning
+; YAML:      Name:            FailedRequestedUnrolling
+; YAML:      Function:        plain_loop
+; YAML:      Args:
+; YAML:        - String:          'loop not unrolled:
+
+; YAML:      --- !Failure
+; YAML:      Pass:            transform-warning
+; YAML:      Name:            FailedRequestedUnrolling
+; YAML:      Function:        vectorizable_l

@@ -839 +844 @@ llvm::UnrollLoop(Loop *L, UnrollLoopOptions ULO, LoopInfo *LI,

+//===-- AssignGUID.cpp - Unique identifier assignment pass ------*- C++ -*-===//
+//
+// Part of the LLVM Project, under the Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions.
+// See https://llvm.org/LICENSE.txt for license information.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+//
+// This file provides a pass which assigns GUID (globally unique identifier)
+// metadata to every GlobalValue in the module, according to its current name,
+// linkage, and originating file. It is idempotent -- if GUID metadata is
+// already present, it does nothing.
+//
+//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
+
+#include "llvm/Transforms/Utils/AssignGUID.h"
+#include "llvm/Support/Debug.h"
+
+using namespace llvm;
+
+void AssignGUIDPass::runOnModule(Module &M) {
+  for (auto &GV : M.globals()) {
+    if (GV.isDeclaration())
+      continue;
+    GV.assignGUID();
+  }
+  for (auto &F : M.functions()) {
+    if (F.isDeclaration())
+      continue;
+    F.assignGUID();
+  }
+}

Summary: This revert changes PredicateInfo's handling of llvm.assume operand bundles to use bundle-op-info/RetainedKnowledge plumbing instead of the older operand_bundles path, and updates related attribute naming and enum checks. It also adds an assume-builder option for preserving all attributes, but the visible behavioral change is concentrated in how assume bundle knowledge is extracted and renamed.
Changed symbols: PredicateInfoBuilder::processAssume; PredicateBase::getConstraint; Attribute::getNameFromAttrKind; ShouldPreserveAllAttributes; isUsefullToPreserve; getKnowledgeFromBundle; RetainedKnowledge; PredicateBundleAssume
Behavioral change: Switches assume-bundle processing from operand_bundles to bundle_op_infos plus getKnowledgeFromBundle.; Changes the predicate attribute kind check from BundleAttr::NonNull to Attribute::NonNull.; Introduces a flag that can preserve more assume attributes during assume building.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA clobber walker verification assertion; ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; OtherClobbers; MSSA.dominates
Reproducer link: -O1 crash involving optimizer memory dependence reasoning
Pass or subsystem link: PredicateInfo; AssumeBundleBuilder; llvm.assume bundle handling

However, the retrieved hunks do not show any MemorySSA updates, clobber-walker code, or explicit dominance fixups, so the link to the reported MemorySSA verification crash is only indirect and not demonstrated by the visible diff.

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp slt i64 [[TMP1]], [[IV_ARG]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP2:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL2:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP2]], i64 [[SEL1]], i64 3

Summary: This commit adds a new LoopStrengthReduce heuristic that merges uses whose fixups are entirely outside the loop with compatible uses inside the loop, and wires that heuristic into the main narrowing pipeline. ; CHECK:       [[LOOP_INC]]:
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[PTR_NEXT]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 16
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[LSR_IV_NEXT]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV_NEXT]], -3
; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND]], label %[[EXIT]], label %[[LOOP]]
; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[TMP1:%.*]] = add i64 [[LSR_IV]], 2
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP1:%.*]] = icmp slt i64 [[TMP1]], [[IV_ARG]]
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP2:%.*]] = icmp eq i64 [[LSR_IV]], -1
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL1:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP1]], i64 1, i64 2
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[SEL2:%.*]] = select i1 [[CMP2]], i64 [[SEL1]], i64 3
; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP:%.*]] = getelementptr i8, ptr [[PTR]], i64 8
; CHECK-NEXT:    store i64 [[SEL2]], ptr [[GEP]], align 8
; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[LSR_IV]]
;
entry:
  br label %loop

loop:
  %ptr = phi ptr [ %ptr.arg, %entry ], [ %ptr.next, %loop.inc ]
  %iv = phi i64 [ %iv.arg, %entry ], [ %iv.next, %loop.inc ]
  %call = call i1 @otherfn(ptr %ptr)
  br i1 %call, label %exit, label %loop.inc

loop.inc:
  %ptr.next = getelementptr i8, ptr %ptr, i64 16
  %iv.next = add i64 %iv, -1
  %exitcond = icmp eq i64 %iv, 0
  br i1 %exitcond, label %exit, label %loop

exit:
  %cmp1 = icmp slt i64 %iv, %iv.arg
  %cmp2 = icmp eq i64 %iv, 1
  %sel1 = select i1 %cmp1, i64 1, i64 2
  %sel2 = select i1 %cmp2, i64 %sel1, i64 3
  %gep = getelementptr i8, ptr %ptr, i64 8
  store i64 %sel2, ptr %gep, align 8
  %sub = add i64 %iv, -2
  ret i64 %sub
}

Summary: This GVN change alters where a rematerialized select is inserted when materializing an adjusted available value for a load. Instead of inserting the new select at the original select's iterator position, it now uses the provided insertion point's iterator, which changes the exact CFG/IR location of the synthesized instruction and can affect dominance and debug-location-sensitive reasoning in GVN's load/select handling.
Changed symbols: AvailableValue::MaterializeAdjustedValue; SelectInst::Create; GVN.cpp; debugloc-load-select.ll; pr69301.ll; pre-load-through-select.ll
Behavioral change: Changes insertion site for a synthesized select from the source select's iterator to the caller-provided InsertPt iterator.; Potentially changes which instruction dominates the newly created select and how later GVN/PRE reasoning observes the rematerialized value.; Does not directly modify MemorySSA, but it touches scalar optimization code that can influence memory-dependence and SSA placement decisions.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA clobber walker verification; ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; OtherClobbers; MSSA.dominates
Reproducer link: Crash at -O1; MemorySSA clobber-walker verification assertion
Pass or subsystem link: GVN; Scalar optimization; MemorySSA-adjacent optimization behavior
Causal explanation: The patch is in GVN rather than MemorySSA, so it is only indirectly related to the reported assertion. Because the issue involves MemorySSA verification and dominance/clobber reasoning, any change that moves synthesized IR instructions can matter if it changes dominance or the shape of optimized loads/selects. However, the retrieved hunks do not show direct MemorySSA updates or verification logic, so the link is plausible but weak.
Causal confidence: 0.31
Build risk: High-risk path: llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/GVN.cpp; Associated tests cover load/select rematerialization and debug-location-sensitive behavior; Patch is labeled NFC, suggesting intended semantic neutrality despite placement change

top_candidates.subject: [ConstantHoisting] Skip PHI edges from unreachable blocks (#203892)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This change makes ConstantHoisting ignore PHI incoming edges whose predecessor blocks are unreachable from the function entry. The patch is narrowly scoped to candidate collection and is paired with a regression test showing that unreachable PHI edges previously triggered assertion failures during constant hoisting.
Changed symbols: ConstantHoistingPass::collectConstantCandidates; PHINode; BasicBlock; DT->isReachableFromEntry; llvm/test/Transforms/ConstantHoisting/AArch64/consthoist-unreachable-phi-edge.ll
Behavioral change: Skips analyzing PHI operands coming from unreachable predecessor blocks when building constant-hoisting candidates.; Avoids trying to rebalance/rebase constants across edges that cannot be reached from entry, which can otherwise distort use/update accounting.; Preserves existing handling for reachable PHI edges and other operand kinds.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA; ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; OtherClobbers; MSSA.dominates
Reproducer link: The retrieved test demonstrates an assertion-failure class bug in a hoisting pass when PHIs have unreachable incoming blocks.; The issue context is an -O1 crash in MemorySSA verification, but this patch only addresses unreachable PHI-edge handling in ConstantHoisting.
Pass or subsystem link: llvm/lib/Transforms/Scalar/ConstantHoisting.cpp; ConstantHoisting
Causal explanation: The patch is plausibly related only at a high level: it fixes a verifier/assertion problem caused by unreachable PHI edges in a scalar optimization that rewrites constants. However, the retrieved hunk does not touch MemorySSA, clobber walking, dominance queries in MemorySSA, or any of the named crash sites from the issue. Based on the available evidence, it is more likely a separate assertion fix than a direct fix for the reported MemorySSA crash.
Causal confidence: 0.22
Build risk: Touches optimization logic in a high-risk scalar pass.; Adds a reachability check that depends on DominatorTree state.; Regression test indicates prior assertion sensitivity around unreachable CFG edges.

+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt < %s -mtriple aarch64-- -passes=consthoist -S | FileCheck %s
+
+; The PHI node has some inbound edges with constants that originate from
+; basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry. Those could be tricky
+; to update when trying to find insertion points etc for a common base
+; constant.
+
+; The test case was added as a regression test to show that that we no longer
+; hit assertion failures about number of users updated/rebased. The workaround
+; is to ignore phi edges from basic blocks that aren't reachable from entry
+; when looking for candidate constants.
+
+define i64 @func(i1 %b0, i1 %b1) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define i64 @func(
+; CHECK-SAME: i1 [[B0:%.*]], i1 [[B1:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B0]], label %[[BLOCK1:.*]], label %[[BLOCK2:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK1]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST1:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK2]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[B1]], label %[[BLOCK3:.*]], label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[BLOCK3]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CONST:%.*]] = bitcast i64 4886718345 to i64
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE1:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[UNREACHABLE2:.*]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[MERGE]]
+; CHECK:       [[MERGE]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[V:%.*]] = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE1]] ], [ 4886718345, %[[UNREACHABLE2]] ], [ [[CONST1]], %[[BLOCK1]] ], [ [[CONST]], %[[BLOCK3]] ], [ 0, %[[BLOCK2]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret i64 [[V]]
+;
+entry:
+  br i1 %b0, label %block1, label %block2
+
+block1:
+  br label %merge
+
+block2:
+  br i1 %b1, label %block3, label %merge
+
+block3:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable1:
+  br label %merge
+
+unreachable2:
+  br label %merge
+
+merge:
+  %v = phi i64 [ 4886718345, %unreachable1 ], [ 4886718345, %unreachable2 ], [ 4886718345, %block1 ], [ 4886718345, %block3 ], [ 0, %block2 ]
+  ret i64 %v
+}

top_candidates.subject: [Loads][LAA] Properly handle multiple deref assumptions (#204083)
top_candidates.diff_summary:
Summary: This commit changes how LLVM combines multiple assumption-derived facts about pointer dereferenceability and alignment. In Loads.cpp it stops caching a single best retained-knowledge record and instead accumulates alignment and dereferenceable evidence independently across assumptions, returning as soon as both facts are proven. In LoopAccessAnalysis it likewise folds each valid dereferenceable assumption into the running SCEV byte-count using UMax, rather than keeping only one retained knowledge entry. The accompanying LoopVectorize test adds coverage for an extra constant-size dereferenceable assume so the new accumulation logic is exercised.
Changed symbols: isDereferenceableAndAlignedPointerViaAssumption; willNotFreeBetween; evaluatePtrAddRecAtMaxBTCWillNotWrap; getKnowledgeForValue; deref_assumption_in_preheader_non_constant_trip_count_access_i8_extra_constant_assume
Behavioral change: Combines multiple alignment/dereferenceable assumptions instead of letting one retained record overwrite or suppress another.; Returns true only after both alignment and dereferenceability are established, while continuing to scan other assumptions until then.; Accumulates dereferenceable byte counts with UMax across all valid assumptions in LoopAccessAnalysis.
Assertion or trace link: MemorySSA clobber walker verification assertion; OtherClobbers; MSSA.dominates; ClobberWalker::verifyOptResult; MemorySSA.cpp
Reproducer link: -O1 crash in MemorySSA clobber-walker verification on a reduced C testcase
Pass or subsystem link: Loads analysis; LoopAccessAnalysis; LoopVectorize

The tests added here cover a perfect-nest guard case and a cold-function phase-ordering case that distinguish the new latch-bypass rewrite from full loop duplication.

+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;

+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]

+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).

+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0

+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:

+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]

new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..6b84b45ef477
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/PhaseOrdering/unswitch-nontrivial-cold-func.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,114 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --scrub-attributes --version 2
+
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=optsize -S | FileCheck %s
+; RUN: opt < %s -passes='pgo-force-function-attrs,function(loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch<nontrivial>))' -pgo-kind=pgo-instr-use-pipeline -pgo-cold-func-opt=minsize -S | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).
+
+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function
+; CHECK-SAME: (i1 [[COND:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) #[[ATTR0:[0-9]+]] {{.*}}{
+; CHECK-NEXT:  entry:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_NOT:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[COND]], label [[IF_THEN:%.*]], label [[IF_ELSE:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       if.then:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_A:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_A:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_A]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_A]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       if.else:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL_B:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC_B:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL_B]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC_B]], ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       loop.latch:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_NOT:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_NOT]], label [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_HEADER]], !prof [[PROF17]]
+; CHECK:       exit.loopexit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       exit:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.not = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.not, label %exit, label %loop.preheader, !prof !17
+
+loop.preheader:
+  br label %loop.header
+
+loop.header:
+  %i = phi i32 [ 0, %loop.preheader ], [ %i.next, %loop.latch ]
+  br i1 %cond, label %if.then, label %if.else
+
+if.then:
+  %gep.a = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %A, i32 %i
+  %val.a = load i32, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  %inc.a = add i32 %val.a, 1
+  store i32 %inc.a, ptr %gep.a, align 4
+  br label %loop.latch
+
+if.else:
+  %gep.b = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr %B, i32 %i
+  %va

diff --git a/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
new file mode 100644
index 000000000000..d08c03e7a31f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/llvm/test/Transforms/SimpleLoopUnswitch/trivial-unswitch-loop-guard.ll
@@ -0,0 +1,1031 @@
+; NOTE: Assertions have been autogenerated by utils/update_test_checks.py UTC_ARGS: --version 6
+; RUN: opt -passes='loop-mssa(simple-loop-unswitch),verify<loops>' -S < %s | FileCheck %s
+
+;; Check that a loop-invariant guard branch in a perfect nest is trivially
+;; unswitched.  The outer loop's header branches to the latch (skipping the
+;; inner loop entirely) when N == 0, or falls through into the inner loop.
+;; Because N is loop-invariant, the new code in unswitchTrivialBranch rewires
+;; the latch arm to point at the outer-loop exit, making the branch look like
+;; an ordinary exit branch and allowing the standard trivial-unswitch logic to
+;; hoist it out of the outer loop.
+;;
+;; Source:
+;;   void f(int M, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
+;;       if (N <= 0) continue;          // invariant guard branches to latch
+;;       for (int i = 0; i < N; i++)
+;;         A[i] = B[i] + 1;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; The key CFG edge is: outer.header --[N==0]--> outer.latch (the latch),
+;; outer.header --[N!=0]--> inner.preheader (inside the outer loop).
+
+define void @perfect_nest_guard(i32 %M, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @perfect_nest_guard(
+; CHECK-SAME: i32 [[M:%.*]], i32 [[N:%.*]], ptr [[A:%.*]], ptr [[B:%.*]]) {
+; CHECK-NEXT:  [[ENTRY:.*:]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[CMP_M:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[M]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_M]], label %[[EXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GUARD:%.*]] = icmp sle i32 [[N]], 0
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[GUARD]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[OUTER_PREHEADER_SPLIT]] ], [ [[J_NEXT:%.*]], %[[OUTER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_PREHEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_PREHEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_HEADER:.*]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_HEADER]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, %[[INNER_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], %[[INNER_LATCH:.*]] ]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_B:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[B]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[VAL:%.*]] = load i32, ptr [[GEP_B]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[INC:%.*]] = add i32 [[VAL]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[GEP_A:%.*]] = getelementptr inbounds i32, ptr [[A]], i32 [[I]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    store i32 [[INC]], ptr [[GEP_A]], align 4
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[INNER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[INNER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[I]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_INNER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[I_NEXT]], [[N]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_INNER]], label %[[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[INNER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[OUTER_LATCH]]
+; CHECK:       [[OUTER_LATCH]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[J_NEXT]] = add nuw i32 [[J]], 1
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[EXITCOND_OUTER:%.*]] = icmp eq i32 [[J_NEXT]], [[M]]
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[EXITCOND_OUTER]], label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT:.*]], label %[[OUTER_HEADER]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT_LOOPEXIT_SPLIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label %[[EXIT]]
+; CHECK:       [[EXIT]]:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    ret void
+;
+entry:
+  %cmp.M = icmp sle i32 %M, 0
+  br i1 %cmp.M, label %exit, label %outer.preheader
+
+outer.preheader:
+  %guard = icmp sle i32 %N, 0
+  br label %outer.header
+
+outer.header:
+  %j = phi i32 [ 0, %outer.preheader ], [ %j.next, %outer.latch ]
+  br i1 %guard, label %outer.latch,

The visible test additions show new handling for dereferenceable loads and assume-derived dereferenceability, indicating a more permissive but context-sensitive speculation rule.

diff --git a/offload/plugins-nextgen/common/src/PluginInterface.cpp b/offload/plugins-nextgen/common/src/PluginInterface.cpp
index 1e05c6ae66fd..f8f362cf2b4e 100644
--- a/offload/plugins-nextgen/common/src/PluginInterface.cpp

+
+;; Check that genuinely non-trivial loop unswitching - where the optimizer
+;; would have to duplicate the entire loop body - is suppressed for cold
+;; (optsize/minsize) functions.
+;;
+;; The branch on %cond in the loop header is loop-invariant, but both of its
+;; successors (if.then, if.else) stay inside the loop, so unswitching it
+;; requires producing two full copies of the loop.  That code-size increase
+;; must be blocked when the function is cold.
+;;
+;; Contrast with unswitch-cold-func.ll, where the invariant condition can be
+;; hoisted via a latch-bypass rewrite that introduces no code duplication and
+;; is therefore allowed even for cold functions.

+;; Source:
+;;   void function(bool cond, int N, int *A, int *B) {
+;;     for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
+;;       if (cond) A[i]++;
+;;       else      B[i]++;
+;;     }
+;;   }
+;; profiled when called with N=0 (cold).

+define void @function(i1 %cond, i32 %N, ptr %A, ptr %B) !prof !16 {
+; CHECK-LABEL: define void @function

+; CHECK-NEXT:    br i1 [[CMP_NOT]], label [[EXIT:%.*]], label [[LOOP_PREHEADER:%.*]], !prof [[PROF17:![0-9]+]]
+; CHECK:       loop.preheader:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    br label [[LOOP_HEADER:%.*]]
+; CHECK:       loop.header:
+; CHECK-NEXT:    [[I:%.*]] = phi i32 [ 0, [[LOOP_PREHEADER]] ], [ [[I_NEXT:%.*]], [[LOOP_LATCH:%.*]] ]

diff --git a/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake b/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
index d09def0afdb7..6e56dfd783d1 100644
--- a/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
+++ b/lldb/cmake/modules/AddLLDB.cmake
@@ -494,0 +495,25 @@ endfunction()
+# PluginManager discovers dynamic script interpreter plugins at runtime by
+# scanning the directory that holds liblldb, so a plugin is loaded only when it
+# sits beside it. A framework build moves liblldb into the bundle, so the plugin
+# must move with it and carry an rpath that reaches liblldb from its new
+# location.
+function(lldb_add_scriptinterpreter_plugin_to_framework name)
+  if(NOT LLDB_BUILD_FRAMEWORK)
+    return()
+  endif()
+  set_property(TARGET ${name} APPEND PROPERTY
+    INSTALL_RPATH "@loader_path/../../..")
+  # Copy under the unversioned name: PluginManager derives a plugin's
+  # initializer symbol from it. A versioned copy would load but never
+  # initialize.
+  set(plugin_in_framework
+    "${LLDB_FRAMEWORK_ABSOLUTE_BUILD_DIR}/LLDB.framework/Versions/${LLDB_FRAMEWORK_VERSION}/$<TARGET_LINKER_FILE_NAME:${name}>")
+  add_custom_command(TARGET ${name} POST_BUILD VERBATIM
+    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E copy "$<TARGET_FILE:${name}>" "${plugin_in_framework}"
+    COMMENT "Copy ${name} into LLDB.framework")
+  add_custom_target(${name}-framework-cleanup
+    COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E remove "${plugin_in_framework}"
+    COMMENT "Removing ${name} from LLDB.framework")
+  add_dependencies(lldb-framework-cleanup ${name}-framework-cleanup)
+endfunction()
+

# Returns TRUE in `out_var` if any of `libs` is `liblldb` or already carries
# the LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB property.
function(_lldb_links_liblldb_check out_var libs)
  set(${out_var} FALSE PARENT_SCOPE)
  foreach(lib ${libs})
    if("${lib}" STREQUAL "liblldb")
      set(${out_var} TRUE PARENT_SCOPE)
      return()
    endif()
    if(TARGET "${lib}")
      get_target_property(_p "${lib}" LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB)
      if(_p)
        set(${out_var} TRUE PARENT_SCOPE)
        return()
      endif()
    endif()
  endforeach()
endfunction()

function(_lldb_propagate_links_liblldb name libs)
  _lldb_links_liblldb_check(_links_liblldb "${libs}")
  set_target_properties(${name} PROPERTIES LLDB_LINKS_LIBLLDB ${_links_liblldb})
endfunction()

function(lldb_record_dynamic_script_interpreter_exports target)
  set(symbol_file
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${target}.undefined.symbols")

  # llvm-nm is registered as a CMake target after the LLDB subdirectory is
  # processed, so a forward target reference is required. LLVM_NM, when set,
  # points to a prebuilt host tool for cross-compiled builds.
  if(LLVM_NM)
    set(nm_exe "${LLVM_NM}")
    set(nm_dep)
  else()
    set(nm_exe "$<TARGET_FILE:llvm-nm>")
    set(nm_dep llvm-nm)
  endif()

  set(extra_args)
  if(APPLE)
    list(APPEND extra_args --mach-o)
  endif()

    OUTPUT ${symbol_file}
    COMMAND "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}"

    COMMAND_EXPAND_LISTS

  add_custom_target(${target}-exports DEPENDS ${symbol_file})

top_candidates.subject: [MLIR][XeGPU] Fix load_matrix lowering for non-LLVM element types (#203629)

Summary: This commit fixes XeGPU-to-XeVM lowering for matrix loads with element types that are not directly representable in LLVM IR. Instead of special-casing only vector-of-one loads, it now asks the type converter for the lowered load type, which maps unsupported element types to integer storage types and preserves the scalar-collapse behavior for single-element vectors. The test adds coverage for f8E8M0FNU scalar and vector loads.
